history.dynasty: Within the Srikalahasti temple complex: Pallava (5th century, per tradition), Chola (11th-12th century), Vijayanagara (Krishnadevaraya, 1516).
history.period: Construction date of this sub-shrine unknown
history.summary: Sub-shrine of the Srikalahasti temple complex (row 1233): a smaller shrine dedicated to Subrahmanya (Kartikeya) is independently listed among the complex's subsidiary shrines alongside Kasi Viswanatha, Annapurna, Suryanarayana and Sadyoganapathi. No standalone history, timings or image specific to this sub-shrine was found - details are shared with the main complex. Coordinates are those of the main Srikalahasti complex; the sub-shrine's exact position is unverified. RELATED ROW: 1233 (main temple).

name: Sri Subrahmanya Swamy Temple
town_description: Srikalahasti, in Tirupati district on the banks of the Swarnamukhi river about 36 km from Tirupati, is an ancient temple town known as the 'Kashi of the South' (Dakshina Kasi). It is famed as a Rahu-Ketu remedial pilgrimage centre and for its hand-crafted Srikalahasti Kalamkari art.
tradition: Shaivism (sub-shrine within a Shaivite temple complex)

travel.road: About 36 km from Tirupati by road (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: Cooler months are generally comfortable for the region (verify)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Same as the main Srikalahasti temple complex: 5:00/6:00 AM - 9:00 PM (verify)
